title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We report a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment that measures the effect of exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow when repairing vendor-CLI configuration candidates corrupted by deterministic controlled faults. Under the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter and shared_controlled_fault_candidate pairing semantics (one deterministic injected candidate reused across arms), we planned 40 confirmatory task pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per preregistered rules). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the deterministic verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts were n11=29, n10=9 (guarded-only), n01=1 (baseline-only), n00=0; the absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Confirmatory execution used the declared model version gpt-5-mini and consumed 118 hosted-model calls (<=120). The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary; the frozen harmful-change mapping and per-episode validator traces needed to compute that aggregation were recorded and enable deterministic independent recomputation. We present the preregistered primary result, justify design and pairing semantics, analyze representative failure modes from archived validation traces, and state limitations and reproducibility guidance without altering the preregistered scientific record.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being investigated as assistants for network operations (NetOps) tasks including intent-to-CLI translation and automated remediation. Practical safety architectures for closed-loop use commonly interpose deterministic verifiers between generation and acceptance and, when violations are found, feed verifier diagnostics back to a generator/repair model (a generate–verify–repair, or GVR, pipeline). Prior controlled and benchmark studies in code and Infrastructure-as-Code report that deterministic verifiers increase verifier-detected pass rates in those domains but also identify new failure modes (e.g., verifier-exploitation) and nontrivial interaction costs. Empirical NetOps field work warns that read-oriented assistance does not by itself justify safe autonomous closed-loop changes. These findings motivate a focused, preregistered controlled-challenge evaluation that uses deterministic fault injection to guarantee intervention activation and a paired design that isolates the effect of exposing verifier diagnostics to the repair model.

Research question and contribution. Our preregistered research question: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) executed under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; (2) an analysis of the primary paired estimand with exact paired testing and bootstrap CI reporting; (3) mechanistic diagnostics grounded in archived per-episode validator traces showing representative failure modes and how diagnostics affect repairs; and (4) a precise statement of unresolved preregistered safety aggregation status and reproducibility guidance.
sections.related_work: Generate–verify–repair pipelines and verifier-mediated refinement have been studied across code, IaC, and domain-specific languages. Controlled pipeline evaluations demonstrate that deterministic verifiers interposed between probabilistic generation and acceptance can increase verifier-detected pass rates and that supplying verifier diagnostics to a repair model can raise the chance a corrected artifact satisfies the verifier on recheck [doi:10.2139/ssrn.6754899, https://openalex.org/W7171267824]. Complementary analyses document caveats: optimization toward a single verifier proxy can produce pathological behaviors (verifier-exploitation) and verifier-mediated workflows impose measurable interaction and compute overheads (the ‘‘verifier tax’’) that depend on horizon and design choices [https://openalex.org/W7171267824, https://openalex.org/W7140238430]. Surveys and field case studies in NetOps/AIOps find that LLMs are useful for read-oriented assistance but that closed-loop autonomous changes require stronger verification and governance to approach production safety expectations [https://openalex.org/W7161165783, https://openalex.org/W7162044117]. Our study addresses a gap identified in these syntheses: controlled-challenge, deterministic fault-injection experiments targeted at vendor-CLI repair under preregistered pairing semantics (see Preregistration section). We do not claim broad operational readiness; instead, we provide a narrowly scoped, execution-grounded measurement of diagnostics exposure under matched budgets and shared initial candidates.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1). The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where success requires agreement between a deterministic vendor-CLI validator and a simulator-based compliance check.

Adapter, pairing, and execution semantics. Confirmatory execution used the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter under its shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics. Under that contract each task index received exactly one deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate which was reused unchanged across both experimental conditions; exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms. Baseline denotes blind repair (repair without exposure of validator diagnostics) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed to the repair model. Because source generation and the injected faulty candidate were shared and each arm received its permitted repair opportunity under the adapter contract, observed between-arm differences isolate the effect of exposing diagnostics under matched repair budgets.

Model sampling and runtime parameters. Confirmatory execution declared model gpt-5-mini. The archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Exactly one sampled initial generation per pair was reused by both arms as required by the adapter semantics; the design therefore does not test independent first-pass sampling differences across conditions.

Controlled fault bank, acceptance predicate, and scoring. Forty controlled-fault task indices (1..40) were deterministically generated by a frozen fault generator and injected into vendor-CLI template candidates. The primary success predicate required both (a) the deterministic vendor-CLI validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) to mark the candidate valid and (b) a simulator-based compliance agreement recorded in the per-episode validation traces. The preregistration also froze a harmful-change labeling mapping (an episode is harmful if post-repair validation contains PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE); this mapping and per-episode validation traces were recorded during execution and enable deterministic independent reaggregation of the preregistered harmful-overrepair statistic (the confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference).

Statistical analysis plan. The predefined primary test was a two-sided exact paired binary test (exact McNemar or equivalent). We report discordant-pair counts (n10, n01), the absolute paired risk difference with a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile confidence interval (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, seed = 1729), and the two-sided exact p-value. Missingness followed the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule (exclude a pair only if both executions are unscorable); sensitivity analyses treating missing episodes as failures were preregistered. All per-episode traces and scored artifacts required to recompute aggregations were recorded during execution.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes correspond to 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per the preregistered rule). Hosted-model calls used = 118 (<= planned maximum 120). Source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline (blind repair) success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded (verifier-guided) success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729).

Discordant-pair structure and interpretive diagnostics. The discordant structure is dominated by guarded-only successes (n10 = 9) with a single baseline-only success (n01 = 1). Representative archived scoring artifacts illustrate plausible mechanisms. Example: pair-000003 (task-000003) is labeled difficulty = hard in the task manifest; baseline produced a post-repair configuration that violated PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE and UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE (validator_trace.violation_codes includes "PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE", "UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE", "FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH") and thus failed the acceptance predicate; the guarded arm, which received validator diagnostics (validator_feedback_exposed_to_model = true), produced a corrected candidate that passed the deterministic validator and simulator checks. Representative artifacts (execution/scoring/task-000003-*.json) show this contrast. Across archived validator traces the most salient violation codes observed in failing baseline episodes include PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE, UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE, and FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH; guarded episodes that succeeded after diagnostics exposure commonly contain validator_trace.violation_codes in the source-phase traces and a validation_after with no violations. These artifacts support a mechanistic reading: exposing concise deterministic violation codes and targeted failure-context appears to guide the repair model to restore required command sequences or avoid protected-field edits that blind repair sometimes omitted or inverted. The archived per-episode traces contain the exact records needed for auditors to verify these representative cases.

Missingness and exclusions. One pair was excluded under the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule because its source generation was invalid/unscorable; terminal error reasons for excluded episodes were recorded in the execution manifest. No confirmatory-stage technical failures of repair calls were reported. Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode accounting consistency (complete_pair_count = 39; see analysis artifacts).
sections.discussion:
Magnitude, precision, and statistical interpretation. The observed paired-estimate (~20.5 percentage points) is statistically detectable with the planned paired exact test (p = 0.02148) and the 95% bootstrap CI excludes zero. The dominance of n10 (guarded-only) discordance indicates the realized effect primarily arises from instances where diagnostics enabled successful repair that blind repair failed to produce under the shared candidate/repaired-budget constraints. Complete_pairs = 39 gives reasonable precision for the observed contrast but limits inference about smaller effects and subgroup heterogeneity.

Why the paired shared-candidate estimand? The shared_controlled_fault_candidate pairing fixes the injected faulty candidate and the initial sampled generation across arms, removing variation arising from independent first-pass generations and ensuring that differences reflect only the presence or absence of diagnostic exposure and any permitted repair-call nondeterminism. This design is appropriate for isolating the treatment of verifier-feedback under a matched repair budget, but it explicitly does not measure effects that would arise from differing initial candidate draws across arms.

Representative failure modes and mitigations. Archived validator traces show recurring failure modes: (a) missing or not-restored required commands (FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH), (b) edits to protected intent fields (PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE), and (c) modifications creating UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE. In representative discordant examples the guarded condition avoided protected-interface edits or reinserted necessary restore commands after receiving explicit violation codes. These findings suggest concrete mitigations: expose structured violation codes rather than free-form natural-language diagnostics, include explicit harmful-change constraints (frozen in this study), and combine multi-verifier checks to reduce single-proxy exploitation risk.

Unresolved preregistered safety aggregation. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation (bounding increases in harmful over-repair) was not present in the archived confirmatory summary produced by the confirmatory analysis executor; therefore the preregistered safety verdict is unresolved for confirmatory inference. The frozen harmful-change mapping and the per-episode validation traces required to compute that aggregation were recorded during execution and enable deterministic independent recomputation; any harmful-overrepair numbers computed outside the archived confirmatory summary must be treated as exploratory.

Operational implications and verifier tax. Exposing deterministic diagnostics materially improved verifier+simulator-validated success on the evaluated controlled-fault bank under matched budgets. Confirmatory execution consumed 118 hosted-model calls; this accounting enables exploratory assessments of per-avoided-failure model-call cost but does not itself determine deployment feasibility. Large-scale operational tradeoffs (latency, cost, orchestration complexity) require broader replication across models, verifiers, and realistic production workloads.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: the shared initial-generation semantics and temperature = null/unset (recorded) mean that nondeterministic model sampling and exactly-one initial draw per pair limit claims about generation determinism and about effects that depend on multiple independent first-pass generations. Construct validity: primary success required agreement of a deterministic validator and a simulator; both artifacts constrain the operational meaning of "valid." External validity: confirmatory execution used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), a synthetic template-based controlled-fault bank, and one adapter family; generalization to diverse vendor equipment, real operator task streams, or different model/tool stacks is limited. Conclusion validity: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable power for the observed effect size but limits precision for subgroup/fault-class inference.

Reproducibility and independent audit. All per-episode traces, scored artifacts, and frozen mappings required to reproduce the primary analysis and to deterministically recompute the preregistered harmful-overrepair statistic were archived in the evidence bundle. Independent auditors can deterministically reaggregate the preregistered safety statistic from those artifacts; until such recomputation appears in an archived confirmatory summary we consider the harmful-overrepair confirmatory test unresolved.
sections.conclusion: In this preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using a hosted validator-feedback repair adapter and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in deterministic verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). The result is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), the deterministic verifier and simulator used in execution, and the shared_controlled_fault_candidate pairing semantics (one sampled initial generation reused across arms). The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference; the frozen harmful-change mapping and the per-episode validation traces recorded during execution provide exact inputs for independent reconstruction of that preregistered safety statistic. We recommend targeted replications across models and verifiers, computation of the preregistered safety aggregation from the archived traces, and larger-scale cost/latency studies to assess operational feasibility and long-horizon exploitation risk in agentic NetOps pipelines.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Adapter family used for confirmatory execution: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini. Exact initial master prompt archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10). Human role and autonomy boundary: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: the archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The preregistered harmful-change labeling mapping used to define the planned safety aggregation was frozen before execution; the mapping and per-episode validation traces required to compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation were recorded during execution. All per-episode traces, scored artifacts, and transformation mappings needed to reproduce the preregistered secondary aggregations were recorded in the archived evidence bundle. The study followed the preregistered stopping rule.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and counts were recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and the frozen mapping required to compute it were recorded and are available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
